description:
An educational 3D Mars survival simulator in which young astronauts conduct scientific experiments and tackle interactive missions to learn how atmospheric pressure, radiation, energy, and food production determine the survival of a Martian colony.

Using scientific data from NASA and simplified simulations of physical and chemical phenomena, players learn through experimentation, observation, and decision-making.
summary:
Imagine being stranded on Mars. 
How would you survive? 
What would happen if your habitat lost pressure, your food supply ran low, or you were exposed to dangerous levels of radiation?

These are some of the questions behind our project: an interactive 3D Mars survival simulator that helps young students discover what it takes to live on another planet.

Built with Three.js and Blender, the simulator lets players explore a Martian habitat, run experiments, and face challenges inspired by real NASA research. Instead of simply reading about atmospheric pressure, radiation, protective shielding, or food production, students can see how these factors affect survival and experiment with different solutions.

The simulator has two modes. 
In Experiments, players explore scientific concepts by changing conditions and observing what happens. In Missions, they put that knowledge to use, solving problems involving habitat safety, limited resources, and astronaut protection.

Our goal is to make space science something students can experience, not just study. By combining realistic scenarios, interactive experiments, and gameplay, we hope to spark curiosity, encourage problem-solving, and inspire more young people to explore science, engineering, and space exploration.
details:
Project Details — Biosfera Marte

Biosfera Marte is an interactive 3D survival game that puts players in the role of Hobson, an astronaut stranded on Mars after a landing accident damages his spacecraft and communication equipment. After four years of isolation, his mission is to survive, restore communication with NASA, repair his rocket, and find a way back home.

The game runs directly in a web browser and allows players to explore a Martian environment in first person. They must manage essential survival needs such as oxygen, water, and food while navigating a challenging environment. Players can explore a space habitat, collect resources, grow carrots inside a greenhouse, repair damaged equipment, and complete missions that gradually lead to the spacecraft's launch.

Our goal is to make space exploration more accessible and engaging through interactive learning. Instead of simply reading about the challenges astronauts face on Mars, players experience a fictional survival scenario in which resource management, exploration, and problem-solving are essential to completing their mission.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js, with 3D objects and procedural terrain rendered directly in the browser. It uses JavaScript modules to organize different systems, including movement, survival, agriculture, communication, and mission progression. The game does not require a backend, database, or specialized hardware. It also supports Portuguese, English, and Spanish, making the experience accessible to a wider audience.

What makes Biosfera Marte creative is its combination of storytelling, exploration, and survival mechanics in a single interactive experience. Rather than presenting isolated educational exercises, the project connects everyday decisions to a larger objective: helping an astronaut survive and return to Earth. Activities such as growing food, managing oxygen, collecting components, and repairing communication systems become meaningful parts of the story.

During development, our team considered accessibility, performance, player engagement, and technical simplicity. We chose a browser-based architecture to reduce barriers to entry and organized the code into independent modules to make future improvements easier. We also introduced multilingual support and improved camera controls to create a more comfortable gameplay experience.

Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space exploration, engineering, and the challenges of living beyond Earth. By combining an immersive environment with interactive problem-solving, Biosfera Marte aims to encourage young people to explore scientific and technological concepts through play.

Although the game includes environmental and survival mechanics inspired by Martian conditions, it is currently an educational game prototype rather than a scientifically validated simulation. Future development could strengthen the connection between its gameplay systems and real NASA scientific data.
